newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa drifts to lows on origin, arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa drifts to lows on origin, arbitrage.

text.p: London cocoa futures slipped to near their lows on Monday as sterling's rally provided fresh impetus for origin and arbitrage selling, traders said.
Futures prices retreated again to technically-oversold territory with RSIs now signalling corrective move but traders said sterling's strength provided little respite from selling.
"Industry needs to buy more in London but it's too expensive for them," said one trader.
Sterling touched a four-year high of $1.6725 on Monday before steadying around $1.6695 in the afternoon.
Benchmark March cocoa finished the day's trade at 914 stg a tonne, just off an earlier low of 913 stg and close to nearby support along a downtrend channel at 910 stg.
If 910 failed, the market could be looking for support at 880, analysts said.
The session recorded minor losses early before taking another pounding after midday.
Exchange turnover totalled 6,911 lots which included a large volume of AAs, crosses and switch trades. March/May was at 17 stg while the distant Dec/March saw good interest at 15 stg.
Traders said the nearby Dec/March spread was likely to weaken further from the present 34 stg as December's expiry neared in the face of abundant spot supplies.
Elsewhere in the physical market industry interest continued on a hand-to-mouth basis with buyers said to be covered for the most part until the end of the first quarter of 1997.
Ivorian cocoa was trading at 15-20 stg under the futures, said one physical trader.
"The only chance you have for a bull move is if the dry period (in Ivory Coast) affects the tail end of the crop," said a futures trader.
Analysts say an unusually dry period in Ivory Coast in October could have damaged the tail of the main crop and reduced the bean size, but no details are yet available.
